_sanitizedExample: This is a SANITIZED EXAMPLE for the public repository, not a live record. Every AWS account id, resource id/ARN, client token and job id below has been replaced with an obviously fictional placeholder; timestamps, S3 object sizes/ETags and the overall shape are preserved to show exactly what a real run of this workflow records and what 91_recreate.sh/40_lambda.sh expect to read from this file. The original, real record stays only in the private development repository.
purpose: Everything needed to recreate the HealthLake datastore after its deletion (cost stop). Recorded BEFORE deletion.

datastore.name: medsafety-fhir-r4
datastore.createClientToken: medsafety-phase3-ds-001 (a NEW token is needed to recreate: this one is bound to the deleted datastore)

importJob.clientToken: medsafety-phase0-v1-import-001 (a NEW token is needed to recreate)

kms.note: kms:ListGrants is not permitted for the deployer role, so HealthLake's grants on the key could not be listed before deletion.

glueLakeFormation.type: resource link created by HealthLake's analytics integration

steps: 1. Confirm the deleted datastore no longer exists; choose NEW client tokens.

2. aws healthlake create-fhir-datastore --datastore-name medsafety-fhir-r4 --datastore-type-version R4 --sse-configuration '{"KmsEncryptionConfig":{"CmkType":"CUSTOMER_MANAGED_KMS_KEY","KmsKeyId":"<kms.keyArn>"}}' --analytics-configuration Status=PAUSED --tags Key=Project,Value=medsafety-intelligence Key=Environment,Value=dev Key=Phase,Value=3 Key=DataClass,Value=synthetic --client-token <new> (authorization AWS_AUTH is the default; analytics DISABLED is rejected at creation)
3. Wait for ACTIVE. The datastore ID and endpoint WILL DIFFER.

4. Fast go/no-go before the full V0-V19: `scripts/healthlake_verify.py --checks V0,V1,V2,V3,V4,V5` (capability statement, one read, identifier search, counts, patient-scoped search, Binary note match).
6. Expect 53 scanned / 53 imported / 0 errors, then re-run 60_verify.sh (V0-V19) and the live golden parity.

5. Full V0-V19 (`scripts/healthlake_verify.py`, no --checks), then Phase 4: infrastructure/aws/api/20_role.sh and 40_lambda.sh (re-render the Lambda role and env with the new datastore ARN/id; no rebuild needed), then scripts/api_verify.py --mode lambda --checks A2,A3,A4,A5,A9,A14 (shortened), then infrastructure/aws/api/60_verify.sh (full A0-A16, A7/A8 stay --pending).
recreate.scripts: infrastructure/aws/healthlake/20_datastore.sh and 50_import.sh do steps 2-3 and 5-6 (change DS_CLIENT_TOKEN / JOB_CLIENT_TOKEN in env.sh first; clear the stale DS_ID/JOB_ID in .state).
recreate.importInputs: the frozen import files in the import bucket (listed above) are byte-identical to data/phase0_v1_0 (SHA256SUMS.txt)
recreate.safeWorkflowTool: infrastructure/aws/healthlake/91_recreate.sh -- read-only preflight (datastore truly gone, CMK enabled + alias intact, 3 IAM roles present, S3 object counts unchanged), refuses to reuse either client token recorded above, backs up then clears the stale DS_ID/DS_ARN/DS_ENDPOINT/DS_CREATED_AT/JOB_ID from .state/deploy.env, then prints the ordered by-hand command plan (steps 2-9 below). It creates nothing itself. RECREATE_DS_CLIENT_TOKEN=<new> RECREATE_JOB_CLIENT_TOKEN=<new> CONFIRM_RECREATE=yes ./91_recreate.sh
recreate.knownFootgunFixed: 50_import.sh previously fell back to a JOB_ID left in .state/deploy.env without checking it belonged to the current datastore; after a delete+recreate that JOB_ID belongs to the OLD (gone) datastore and describe-fhir-import-job would target the wrong datastore. Fixed: the job id is always re-resolved live, scoped to the current DS_ID (test: tests/unit/test_aws_scripts.py::test_import_never_trusts_a_job_id_left_in_state_by_a_previous_deleted_datastore).

deletion.command: aws healthlake delete-fhir-datastore --datastore-id 00000000000000000000000000000002 (deployer role MedSafetyPhase3DeployerRole; 90_teardown.sh was NOT run)
removedAutomaticallyByAws: the HealthLake-created Glue resource-link database medsafety_fhir_r4_<id>_healthlake_view
the Lake Formation permissions that referenced that database (0 permission entries remain)
deletion.unchanged: KMS key (Enabled, alias kept, key policy unchanged), both S3 buckets (objects identical: key/size/etag), all five MedSafety IAM roles, Phase 4 Lambda/DynamoDB/API Gateway/log group
deletion.notVerifiable: KMS grants created by HealthLake (kms:ListGrants denied to the deployer); RAM shares (ram:GetResourceShares denied); billing (no Cost Explorer access)

secondLifecycle.note: This section records the SECOND lifecycle (recreation) using 91_recreate.sh and the plan above, unchanged in this file. The original 'datastore'/'importJob'/'s3ObjectsAtRecordTime'/'deletion' sections above are the immutable historical record of the FIRST lifecycle and are not modified.

datastore.note: New id, as expected -- never the deleted 00000000000000000000000000000002. Same CMK, R4, AWS_AUTH, analytics PAUSED, NLP DISABLED, same tags.

clientTokensUsed.note: Both are new UUIDs, neither equal to the tokens recorded above for the deleted datastore/job (91_recreate.sh verified this before proceeding).

verification.deterministicLiveParity: 13/13 passed (tests/live_aws, P001-P010 + patient list + golden outcomes + no-write confirmation)

iamUpdatedToTheNewDatastoreArn: MedSafetyApiLambdaRole (BaseAccess -- also gained healthlake:GetCapabilities, a genuine gap found live; see docs/CHANGE_LOG.md)
secondLifecycle.deletedIdReferenceSweep: confirmed absent from all four live IAM roles' trust/policies and from active local state; intentionally retained only in this file's historical sections above and in test fixtures/docs/CHANGE_LOG.md/docs/PHASE3_HEALTHLAKE.md

glueLakeFormation.note: Auto-recreated by HealthLake itself for the new datastore id, mirroring what was auto-removed on deletion (see 'deletion.removedAutomaticallyByAws' above); not explicitly enabled by any script in this repo.

secondLifecycle.openaiDeployment: The OpenAI (gpt-5.6-luna) Phase 5 deployment (ADR-0011, docs/PHASE5_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT.md) was executed against this same recreation, re-pointing MedSafetyApiLambdaRole and the Lambda's HEALTHLAKE_DATASTORE_ID at this new datastore in the same pass.
secondLifecycle.datastoreStatusAtEndOfThisSession: ACTIVE -- deletion explicitly withheld per instruction; requires separate explicit approval before any future teardown.
